headings: This, that and that one over there
examples: Ovaj hleb je svež.~Ovaj hljeb je svjež.
notes: Serbian has three words where English has two: {ovaj} (this, near me), {taj} (that, near you or just mentioned) and {onaj} (that over there). Each one changes with the noun: {ovaj} grad, {ova} kuća, {ovo} selo.

Engleski ima samo dve reči: “this” (ovaj) i “that” (taj i onaj). U množini su “these” i “those”. Ne menjaju se po rodu.~Engleski ima samo dvije riječi: “this” (ovaj) i “that” (taj i onaj). U množini su “these” i “those”. Ne mijenjaju se po rodu.
Serbian uses a double negative: {Ništa ne vidim} is literally "nothing I don't see". With {niko}, {ništa}, {nikad} and {nijedan}, always keep {ne} or {nije} with the verb.
U engleskom se koristi samo jedna negacija: “I don't see anything” ili “I see nothing”, a nikada “I don't see nothing”.

examples: Cela porodica je ovde.~Cijela porodica je ovdje.
notes: {Ceo} (ekavian) and {cio} (ijekavian) mean "whole". The feminine is {cela} or {cijela}, the neuter {celo} or {cijelo}.
“The whole” ili “all” stoji ispred imenice: “the whole day”, “all day”.

examples: to read → I read, you read, he reads
to speak → I speak, you speak, she speaks
notes: The ending of the infinitive tells you the pattern: {-ati} verbs take {-am, -aš, -a}; {-iti} and most {-eti} verbs take {-im, -iš, -i}; {-ovati} verbs change to {-ujem, -uješ, -uje}: {putovati → putujem}.

U engleskom se glagol skoro ne menja: “I read, you read”, samo u trećem licu jednine dobija -s: “she reads”.~U engleskom se glagol skoro ne mijenja: “I read, you read”, samo u trećem licu jednine dobija -s: “she reads”.

examples: to go → I go / I am going
notes: Learn these as single words: {idem} (I go), {mogu} (I can), {hoću} (I want), {jedem} (I eat), {pijem} (I drink).
Za radnju koja se dešava sada engleski koristi “am/is/are” + -ing: “I am reading”. Srpski ima samo jedan oblik: čitam.
Make a question with {da li} at the start, or put {li} after the verb: {Slušaš li muziku?} Say no by putting {ne} before the verb: {ne znam}.
Pitanja i odrične rečenice u engleskom grade se sa “do/does”: “Do you understand?”, “I don't know.”~Pitanja i odrične rečenice u engleskom grade se sa “do/does”: “Do you understand?”, “I don't know.”

headings: How the past tense is built
examples: Radila sam ceo dan.~Radila sam cio dan.
notes: Serbian past = a short form of {biti} ({sam, si, je, smo, ste, su}) + the past form of the verb. The past form shows gender: a man says {radio sam}, a woman says {radila sam}; plural {radili smo}.

Engleski prošli oblik ne zavisi od roda: “I worked” kaže i muškarac i žena. Pravilni glagoli dobijaju -ed: work → worked, watch → watched.~Engleski prošli oblik ne zavisi od roda: “I worked” kaže i muškarac i žena. Pravilni glagoli dobijaju -ed: work → worked, watch → watched.
Verbs in {-eti} end in {-eo} in ekavian ({video, voleo}) and {-io} in ijekavian ({vidio, volio}). Learn {išao} (went), {došao} (came), {jeo} (ate) and {pio} (drank) as words of their own.
Mnogi česti glagoli su nepravilni: go → went, come → came, eat → ate, drink → drank, see → saw, be → was/were.
For no, use {nisam, nisi, nije, nismo, niste, nisu} instead of {sam, si, je…}: {nisam razumeo}. For a question, start with {Jesi li} or {Da li si}.

U odričnim rečenicama i pitanjima engleski koristi “did”, a glagol ostaje u osnovnom obliku: “I didn't eat”, “Did you see Ana?”~U odričnim rečenicama i pitanjima engleski koristi “did”, a glagol ostaje u osnovnom obliku: “I didn't eat”, “Did you see Ana?”
